I’ve never wanted a child who just nods along, and I won’t want an adult child who does either. Real respect has room for honest disagreement; that’s what makes it real.

This matters enough that God made it one of the Ten Commandments: “Honor your father and mother.” Notice He didn’t put an expiration date on it. The way you honor me will change as you grow — from obeying, to respecting, to one day maybe caring for me the way I once cared for you — but the honor itself is meant to last a lifetime.

So let’s build it together: a relationship rooted in respect, strong enough to hold disagreement, and warm enough to last the rest of our lives. That’s one of the greatest gifts we could ever give each other.
bible_verse_text: Honor your father and your mother, so that you may live long in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
quote_text: An injury is much sooner forgotten than an insult.

title: Working Hard
reference_content:
Here’s one of the most encouraging truths I can give you: hard work requires no intelligence, no money, no advantages, and no connections. It doesn’t matter who your parents are, what you were born with, or how you compare to anyone else. Effort is the one path to success that is completely available to you, every single day. All it asks for is commitment and perseverance — and those are choices, not gifts.

Your ability to work hard in school will be a huge advantage to you for the rest of your life — and not just in a career. Once you’ve learned how to truly work at something, you can apply that same effort to the things that matter most: your marriage someday, raising your kids, staying close to your friends, and above all, your relationship with Christ. Hard work isn’t just for jobs. It’s for everything worth having, because nothing worth having comes easy.

You have real talent and real skills. When you combine them with genuine effort, there’s very little you can’t accomplish if you set your mind to it. But here’s the part most people miss: it isn’t only about how hard you work — it’s about what you work hard on. It all comes down to your priorities.

So let me give you an order worth keeping for life. Put your effort and your priority into these, in this sequence: first your relationship with Christ, then your family (and once you’re married, your spouse comes first, even before your parents and children), then your health, then your work or school, and then your friends. All of them matter. But when you keep them in that order, everything tends to fall into place. When you get the order backwards, even good things start to crowd out the most important ones.

Work hard. Work hard on the right things, in the right order. Do that, and you will not just succeed — you’ll build a life that actually means something.
bible_verse_text: One who is slack in his work is brother to one who destroys.
quote_text: Hard work beats talent when talent doesn’t work hard.

title: Strike One...you're out.
reference_content:
Read this one as carefully as anything I’ve ever told you: never, ever raise a hand against a woman. Not under any circumstance, not for any reason, not one single time. There is no provocation, no argument, no bad day, no “she pushed me to it” that will ever make it okay. None. This is an absolute, for your entire life.

Here’s something you need to understand ahead of time: no one on earth will ever be able to get under your skin like a woman you love. It’s just true. The people closest to our hearts can stir up feelings — including anger — that no stranger ever could. You won’t fully grasp this until you’re in it someday, but when that moment comes and the anger rises, you already know the answer: walk away. Leave the room. Cool down. Nothing bad happens when you walk away. Everything bad happens when you don’t.

Some men carry a temper that runs hot, and some don’t — but the rule is exactly the same either way. If you ever find that your anger scares you, or that you feel close to that line, take it seriously and get help immediately. Talk to a counselor. Talk to me. Talk to a Godly man you trust. Do whatever it takes. Getting help isn’t weak — it’s one of the strongest, most responsible things a man can ever do, and it could save the people you love, and save you.

And understand the stakes plainly, because they’re real: if you ever do it, even once, it’s over. She will be gone — as she should be — and more than likely, you’ll be in jail. One moment can end your marriage, your family, your freedom, and the man you wanted to be.

So decide now, long before you’re ever tested: you will be a man who protects women, never one who harms them. Walk away every single time. There is no strike two here. This is the one line you never, ever cross.
bible_verse_text: A fool always loses his temper, but a wise man holds it back.
quote_text: The worst tempered people I've ever met were the people who knew they were wrong.

title: Money is a Tool
reference_content:
Money is a tool — nothing more, nothing less. You work to live, not live to work. Any other idea about money will only bring you pain and heartache someday. Money doesn’t make you a better person or a worse one. It can’t buy happiness; the most it can buy is a feeling of financial security. And while knowing you’re not headed for the poor house is genuinely nice, that feeling alone will never fill your life or your heart.

Think about what a tool actually is. A hammer is wonderful for building a house and useless for making you happy. Money is exactly the same. Use it for what it’s good for — providing, building, blessing, helping — and don’t ask it to do the things only God and people can do. The moment you expect money to give you peace, worth, or love, it will fail you, because that was never its job.

So be open-handed with it. Give it to God first, then to your family, then to friends and to people and causes in need — in that order. Generosity is the surest sign that money is your tool and not your master. If you grip it too tightly, one of two things happens: you lose it, or worse, you spend your whole life afraid of losing it, which is its own kind of poverty.

Hold money loosely. Earn it honestly, use it wisely, give it freely, and never let it become the thing you measure yourself by. There will always be people with more and people with less, and none of that will tell you a single true thing about your worth.

Here’s the whole chapter in one line: money is not important. It is serious — it deserves your attention and your care — but it is not important. Don’t ever confuse the two.
bible_verse_text: As goods increase, so do those who consume them. And what benefit are they to the owners except to feast their eyes on them?
quote_text: A wise man should have money in his head; not in his heart.

title: New College Friends
reference_content:
Your friends are a reflection of who you are and what you do. We can’t really live without them — and if we pick the wrong ones, sometimes we barely live at all. So pick great friends in college, and be a great friend in return.

Here’s the most important thing I can tell you on this subject: actively look for Christian friends who genuinely love Jesus. Not people who just say they’re Christian, or grew up going to church — look for the ones whose faith is real and alive, who love the Lord and let it show in how they treat people. Those friends will do something no one else can: they’ll point you back toward God when you drift, pray with you when things get hard, and celebrate with you in a way that’s rooted in something eternal. Seek them out on purpose. They are worth more than any other kind of friend you’ll make.

Real friends are with you through the good and the bad. They know you, accept you as you are, and care enough to correct you when you need it — always making sure you understand they love you just the same. College will hand you a whole new set of people to choose from, so choose very, very wisely, because friends will influence you one way or the other. You’ll meet people who grew up in completely different worlds than you did — some in better environments, some in worse. Make sure the ones you pull close build you up and bring you joy, and make sure you do the same for them.

Almost everyone, at some point, gets tangled up with a friend who’s bad for them. You can usually feel that it’s wrong, but by the time you notice, you’ve already let them close, and letting go feels impossible. Watch out especially for the people who seem like they’ve “lived more” — done wilder, riskier things and come out fine. Here’s the truth: they didn’t live more. They dodged a bullet. And the next time, they might not — and the first time you try it, you might not either. Before you follow anyone down that road, ask yourself two honest questions: Can you live with the consequences? And do you want to?

So let go of bad friends — better yet, don’t start with them. And someday, I’d truly love to get to know the good friends you make. Bring them around. Nothing would make me happier.
bible_verse_text: One who has unreliable friends soon comes to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
quote_text: The only reward of virtue is virtue; the only way to have a friend is to be one.

title: The Bible
reference_content:
There’s something a little funny — and a little humbling — about spending all this time giving you my advice, hoping you’ll read every word. Because the honest truth is this: you’d be far better off setting this whole book down and just reading the Bible instead. That goes for everything I say, and everything every other man and woman on earth has ever said — including you. Next to God’s wisdom, all of us are working with tiny, cloudy little perspectives.

At your age, you’ve seen very little of this world. I’ve seen more than you — and I still know almost nothing. That’s not false modesty; it’s just true.

There’s a story I love about this. Two men were arguing, and one insisted there was no God. After going back and forth for a while, the other man pulled out a paper plate and said, “Imagine all the knowledge that could ever exist — everything that could possibly be known about this world — is represented by this plate. How much of it do you think you know?” The first man took a pen and made a single tiny dot. The other man smiled and said, “Don’t you think, somewhere in all the rest of that plate, there just might be something you don’t know — something that could make you wrong?”

That’s the whole thing, really. We know so little, and God knows all of it. So read His Word. Not once — over and over, for the rest of your life. It will teach you, correct you, comfort you, and steady you in ways nothing I write ever could.

I’m grateful you’re reading these pages, and I know it’s because you love me — that’s the only reason I get to share these life lessons with you at all. But please hear me clearly: it’s all garbage compared to what God has to say. My deepest hope is that my advice simply echoes His. You already know that’s true. I just needed to say it out loud, and to make sure you knew that I know it too.
bible_verse_text: All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness.
quote_text: You can learn more about human nature by reading the Bible than by living in New York

title: A Great Communicator
reference_content:
Communication is the key to almost everything you’ll do. It shapes your relationships with your family, your friends, your coworkers, your teachers — everyone. If you want the kind of success and the kind of life you dream about, you’ll have to become a great communicator. It doesn’t matter whether you’re a person of few words or many; what matters is that you learn to connect with people clearly, honestly, and kindly. Let me give you three kinds worth mastering.

**Respectful communication.** This is the foundation. Acknowledge people when they walk into a room. Look them in the eye. Offer a strong handshake. Recognize how someone is feeling, and take it seriously. Call people back when you say you will. These small things tell people they matter — and how you make people feel is something they never forget.

**Truthful communication.** Tell people the truth, but always in love. That means not lying, and not dodging hard conversations just because they’re uncomfortable. It means being kind with your words — honest without being harsh or cruel. It means telling people what they need to know in time for it to matter. And it means being someone who can keep a confidence: a person whose word is good, who doesn’t traffic in gossip, who can be trusted with what’s private.

**Loving communication.** This is the one most men neglect, and it’s the most important of all. A lot of guys are taught, without anyone ever saying it out loud, that expressing love is a weakness. It isn’t — it’s strength. Tell the people you love that you love them, out loud and often. Make the time and effort to truly connect with them, not just pass by them. Be the one who reaches out first, who picks up the phone, who says the thing that’s easy to feel but hard to say. Love that stays silent doesn’t do anyone much good.

Master these three, and you’ll open almost every door worth walking through — in your work, your friendships, and most of all, your family.
bible_verse_text: The Spirit of the Lord spoke through me; his word was on my tongue.
quote_text: Communication is not only the essence of being human, but also a vital property of life.

title: I Love you Anyway
reference_content:
“I love you.” Those may be the most powerful words on earth. For a lot of people, they’re like oxygen — you don’t realize how much you need to hear them until you’re not getting them. Here’s something important to understand early: love is a choice, not a feeling. It’s an action, a decision to love someone right where they are, on their best days and their worst.

I once saw a skit at church that has stuck with me ever since. It laid out three ways people say “I love you,” and only one of them is real:

**Wrong — “I love you BECAUSE…”** you love me, you behave, you’re smart, you don’t talk back. That’s love with a reason, and reasons can change.

**Wrong — “I love you IF…”** you get good grades, you agree with me, you do what I want. That’s love with a condition, and conditions can be failed.

**Right — “I love you ANYWAY.”** No matter what. There is nothing you could ever do to make me stop loving you.

That’s how I love you — anyway, always, no matter what. And it’s how I hope you’ll learn to love others. When your love comes with a “because” or an “if,” it gets complicated and it quietly wounds the people who most need to feel secure with you. Love that has no conditions is the only kind that actually holds.

So love people anyway. And tell them — out loud, all the time. It makes a bigger difference than you can imagine. It doesn’t even matter if you’re mad or hurt in the moment; you can still love someone you’re angry with. It might be a little harder that day, but the love is still there, still a choice, still yours to give.
bible_verse_text: Love always protects, always trusts, always hopes, always perseveres.
quote_text: Love and a cough cannot be hid.

title: Consequences
reference_content:
For everything we do on this earth — and for some things done to us — there are consequences. Sometimes they’re good, sometimes bad, but they always come. And here’s what changes as you grow up: the consequences get bigger. As an adult, you have far more freedom to act, which means far more power to create consequences — for yourself and for everyone around you.

Look at how the stakes rise from childhood to adulthood:

As a child, if you misbehave, you get grounded. As an adult, if you break the law, you go to prison.

As a child, if you crash the car, your parents pay for it. As an adult, you pay — and depending on what happened, the cost can be far steeper than money.

As a child, if you wander off to the wrong place, you might get lost or scolded. As an adult, the wrong place at the wrong time can put you in real danger.

Now let me give you one specific, serious example that too many young men never see coming — and it can destroy a life. The day you turn 18, the law changes for you overnight. If you’re 18 and dating a girl who is under 18 — even by a little, even if you truly love each other, even if nothing at all has changed but the calendar — you can suddenly be committing a crime. A relationship that was completely fine the day before your birthday can now land you in jail and label you a registered sex offender for the rest of your life. That label follows you forever — where you can live, work, and go. The law does not care that it felt innocent, or that she’s your girlfriend. It only cares about the ages.

You get the point. The freedom of adulthood is wonderful, but it carries real weight. You’ve watched me live out the consequences of my own choices — good and bad — and seen how they rippled out to others, too. That’s how consequences work: they rarely stay contained to the person who caused them.

Here’s the most important thing to remember: you can’t always see or measure the consequences before you act. So move thoughtfully. Keep one eye on where your choices lead, and always consider the impact they’ll have — not just on you, but on everyone your life touches.
bible_verse_text: Remember this: whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.
quote_text: You can do anything in this world if you’re prepared to take the consequences.

title: Treating the Things You Own
reference_content:
One of the clearest signs of a person who’s truly grateful for what they have is how well they take care of it. It sounds small, but it isn’t. The way you treat whatever is in your hands quietly reveals the way you see everything — as a gift to be honored, or as something disposable. And I’ll be the first to admit this is an area where I can do better too. So we’re learning this one together.

Practically, this means taking care of whatever you have — your clothes, your phone, a car, your home, your money, and most of all your body, which is the most important thing you’ll ever be trusted to care for. And here’s the heart of it: you take care of things well regardless of what they are. An old, beat-up car gets treated with just as much care as a brand-new one. Modest or fancy, big or small, new or worn out — it doesn’t matter. You care for what you have because caring for it is right, not because of what it’s worth or what it might get you.

This isn’t just my opinion — it’s a biblical principle. Again and again, Scripture teaches that the person who is faithful with a little is trusted with more, and that how we handle what we’ve been given matters deeply to God. Jesus told a whole parable about it. Being faithful in small things is how you’re shaped into someone who can be trusted with big ones.

In Christian language, this idea has a name: stewardship. It means understanding that nothing you have is ultimately yours — it’s on loan from God, entrusted to your care for a while. Your money, your job, your responsibilities, your relationships, even your children someday.

So take care of what’s in your hands — not out of vanity, and not to get more, but out of gratitude. Be a great steward of everything, big and small. It’s one of the quietest, truest ways to say “thank You” to the God who gave it all in the first place.
bible_verse_text: Whoever has will be given more, and they will have an abundance. Whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken from them.
quote_text: Property has its duties as well as its rights.

title: Sometimes No Advice is Better
reference_content:
When you are right in the middle of God’s will, you know it by the Bible, by prayer, and by those around you who are Godly and have wisdom. Stay there and keep your path.

Don’t listen to anyone else, **including me**.
bible_verse_text: I can do all things through Christ, who gives me strength.
quote_text: I know God will not give me anything I can't handle. I just wish that He didn't trust me so much.

title: Pornography II
reference_content:
This is a subject that needs a little more discussion, because it comes in many forms — the internet, magazines, and so-called “men’s clubs.” Stay out of all of them, but let me talk about that last one specifically, because someday you’ll almost certainly get invited, and I want you ready to say no.

If you ever do go, remember this: every woman in that room is someone’s daughter, someone’s sister, maybe someone’s wife or mom. They may insist it doesn’t affect them, that it’s “just for the money” — but that isn’t the truth. Anyone willing to take their clothes off for money in front of strangers is carrying real pain, whether they’ll admit it or not. Don’t let anyone convince you it’s harmless fun. It isn’t, for them or for you.

<review>I’ll be honest with you, because I’d rather you hear it from me: I wish I could say I’ve never set foot in one, but I have. There’s a whole culture, especially in business, that treats these places as normal — a place to close a deal. It’s wrong, and I regret every time I went along with it. I’m telling you so you can do better than I did.</review>

Here’s the deepest problem: like so much else, it isn’t real. Men pay women to act interested in them for a little while. They hand over money to people who care nothing about them beyond their wallet. Men who get hooked on it — and they do — end up paying for fake relationships while avoiding real ones. There’s an old saying about these places: you leave your money there, you leave your dignity there, and the women don’t come home with you either. You walk out with nothing.

And if you ever find yourself pulled toward any of this and struggling to stop, don’t fight it alone in the dark. Come talk to me, or to another Godly man you trust. There’s no shame that grace can’t cover, and this is a battle no man should fight by himself.
bible_verse_text: I made a covenant with my eyes not to look lustfully at a young woman.
quote_text: The true test of a man’s character is what he does when no one is watching.

title: Embarrassment
reference_content:
Almost as destructive as fear, anger, or arrogance is letting embarrassment run your life. This is an area I’ve always struggled with, and it has genuinely cost me. I won’t tell you not to feel embarrassed — that’s nearly impossible, we’re wired for it. What I’ll tell you is this: don’t let it control you or make your decisions for you.

I can remember so many times I missed out on something simply because I was embarrassed, or afraid I might be. Here’s an honest one: there were times I didn’t ask someone out because I was scared of being embarrassed if they said no. And the strange part? It wasn’t really the rejection I feared — it was other people knowing I’d been rejected. Pretty silly when I say it out loud, isn’t it? But that’s exactly how embarrassment works: it magnifies what other people think until it’s bigger than what you actually want.

You know people who don’t seem to get embarrassed by anything. Maybe, from your point of view or mine, there are a few things they should be a little embarrassed about! But look closer: they don’t let other people’s opinions dictate what they say, who their friends are, what they wear, or what they love. And quite frankly? They seem to carry so much less baggage than everyone else. There’s real freedom in that.

Here’s the truth worth remembering: the vast majority of the embarrassment we feel is completely false — a fear of judgment that mostly lives in our own heads. Most people are far too busy worrying about themselves to be thinking about you at all.

So let me ask you to sit with two questions. What actually embarrasses you? Be honest — name the things you avoid, the moments you shrink back from, the stuff you’d never want people to see. And then the more important one: should it? When you really look at each thing, is it worth the power you’ve handed it? More often than not, you’ll find the answer is no — and just seeing that can start to set you free.

There are so many amazing things you’ll get to do and experience in this life. Don’t let the fear of a little embarrassment hold you back from any of them. Feel it if you must — then go do the thing anyway. It is never worth what you’d miss.
bible_verse_text: For you have been my hope, Sovereign Lord, my confidence since my youth.
quote_text: If you're never scared or embarrassed or hurt, it means you never take any chances.

title: Love Language
reference_content:
Tell people, show people, and remind people that you love them. It’s one of the simplest and most powerful things you’ll ever do, and most people don’t do nearly enough of it.

First, tell them — out loud, in actual words. Tell the people you love that you love them: your family, your closest friends, and someday your wife. Don’t assume they just know. Make sure everyone in your family hears it from you regularly. Tell your parents you love them, all the time. Words are free, they take two seconds, and they can carry someone through a hard day.

But telling isn’t the whole picture, because people receive love in different ways. A counselor named Gary Chapman wrote a wonderful book explaining that there are five “love languages” — five different ways people most feel loved:

**Words of Affirmation** — hearing kind, encouraging, specific words.

**Gifts** — receiving something thoughtful, a sign they were thought of.

**Quality Time** — someone giving them their full, undistracted attention.

**Acts of Service** — someone doing something helpful for them.

**Physical Touch** — a hug, a hand on the shoulder (and someday, with your wife, the closeness of marriage).

Here’s the key: everyone has a primary love language, and some people have two. The trick is that we tend to give love in our own language, when the person in front of us might need it in a completely different one. You might feel most loved by quality time, while your friend feels it through words, and your future spouse through acts of service. So pay attention. Learn the love languages of the people closest to you — and then love them their way, not just yours.

Do that, and you’ll love people in a way they can actually feel. It’s one of the great secrets to every close relationship you’ll ever have.

P.S. — You can tell me you love me too!
bible_verse_text: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.
quote_text: Love conquers all things; let us too surrender to love.

title: Alcohol, Drugs and Tobacco
reference_content:
Don’t drink and drive. I know it sounds simple, but I mean it — don’t. And don’t ride with other people who have been drinking, either. I did both, and it is by the sheer grace of God that I’m alive to write this. If even one of those nights had gone wrong, it would have wrecked my life and other people’s lives forever. You will get the chance to make that choice. The risk is never worth it.

The simplest advice about alcohol, drugs, and cigarettes is to stay away, and I hope so far you have. Here’s the trap: you can’t know whether you have an addictive streak until it’s too late to undo it. Some people get hooked far faster than others, and no one thinks it’ll be them. Stay away, and you never carry that risk at all.

I want to say something specifically about drugs, because the world is far more dangerous now than it was when I was young. It used to be that experimenting was risky. Today it can be deadly the very first time. People are putting powerful, lethal substances into pills and powders that look completely normal — so you cannot trust that anything is what someone tells you it is. A single bad decision, or one moment of trusting the wrong person, can end everything. There is no “just once” that is worth that. Please don’t take the chance. I need you here.

A word on cigarettes and vaping, too. Vaping gets sold as harmless, but it’s one of the fastest ways there is to get hooked on nicotine — I’ve watched it grab people hard and quick. And I’ve seen too many smart people stay trapped by cigarettes for decades because they simply can’t stop. Never hand anything that kind of power over you.

One last thing, man to man: so much of this comes down to self-control. When you lose control of your body and your mind, you become capable of things the real you would never do — hurting someone, wrecking a relationship, making a choice you can’t take back. Be a man who stays in control of himself. It protects you, it protects everyone around you, and it’s one of the truest marks of real strength.
bible_verse_text: Wine is a mocker and beer a brawler; whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
quote_text: The best way to avoid a bad habit is to never begin it.

title: Jesus is Lord and Savior
reference_content:
This may be the most important chapter in this entire book, so read it slowly. The whole Christian life comes down to two words in the title — Savior and Lord — and they mean two different things.

The Savior part is a decision. It’s the moment you accept Christ, admit you can’t save yourself, and submit to Him. That’s how you’re forgiven, and that’s how you get to heaven. It’s a gift you receive, not a prize you earn — you simply say yes. If you’ve never truly made that decision, I hope with all my heart that you will. Nothing matters more.

The Lord part is harder, and it lasts a lifetime. That’s when you actually try to live your life to please Him — day by day, choice by choice. You do it out of gratitude, because once you really see it, you realize everything good in your life is a gift: your mind, your health, your family, your home, the country you were born into, the opportunities in front of you — it is all by the grace of God. You didn’t earn any of it. It was given.

He is bigger than any problem you will ever face. Let me say that again, because you’ll need it someday: He is bigger than any problem you will ever face. When you center your life on His standards, you have something solid that never moves. Center it on your own, and the ground keeps shifting under you.

So live by His standards — not out of fear or obligation, but to please the God who made you and loves you. And here’s the beautiful part: since He designed you, when you live His way, you’re finally running the way you were built to run. There’s a peace and a rightness in living as your Maker intended that you simply can’t find anywhere else.

Savior first. Then Lord, for the rest of your life. Everything else in this book is just details next to this.
bible_verse_text: Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
quote_text: A man who was merely a man and said the sort of things Jesus said would not be a great moral teacher. He would either be a lunatic — or else the Devil of Hell.

title: Love and Favor
reference_content:
I’ve wrestled for a long time with the idea of unconditional love. You’ve heard us say it your whole life — we love you unconditionally, meaning no matter what you ever do, our love for you will never change. That’s completely true. I love you, and I always will, no matter what.

But I want to draw an important distinction for you — between love and favor — because they’re not the same thing. You’ve heard the old joke, “I love you, but I don’t always like you.” There’s also the saying, “Love the sinner, hate the sin.” Here’s the deeper version: I can love you unconditionally and completely, and yet you may or may not have favor with me at any given moment. And it works both ways.

Here’s what I mean. If you’re disrespectful, unkind to the people you should honor, careless about staying connected to your family, sloppy with your responsibilities, or you get yourself into trouble — I will still love you with everything I have. But you may not have my favor. And favor comes with real, tangible things: trust, freedom, opportunities, help when you need it, the benefit of the doubt. Lose favor, and some of those things quietly go away. Earn it, and doors open.

That’s the key truth: love is unconditional, but favor is earned. And you’re earning or losing it every single day — with me, with your teachers, with other adults, with everyone whose respect matters. The way you treat people, the way you handle your responsibilities, the way you carry yourself — it’s all quietly building or spending your favor with the world.

This works with God, too, in a way. His love for you is boundless and unconditional — but Scripture is full of the blessings and favor that come to those who walk in His ways.

So earn favor — with those you love and even those you don’t. The rewards are real, and life goes far more smoothly for the person who has it. Love is a gift. Favor is a harvest.
bible_verse_text: Let love and faithfulness never leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart. Then you will win favor and a good name in the sight of God and man.
quote_text: You reap what you sow; more than you sow, and later than you sow.

title: Fear
reference_content:
Fear is one word that will imprison you if you don’t fight it, and keep fighting it, all your life. The first step is simply to be aware of when you’re afraid — to notice it, name it, and see it for what it really is. You’ve heard me say it before, and I’ll say it again: face your fears. I’m sure certain people come to mind right now when you think of someone ruled by fear. Don’t become one of them.

Fear, left unchecked, can quietly wreck a whole life. People afraid of flying never see the world. People afraid to trust never let anyone close enough to truly love them. People afraid of not having a paycheck stay in dead-end jobs for decades, slowly dying a little each day. In almost every case, the fear costs them far more than the thing they were afraid of ever could have.

Here’s something worth understanding: most fear isn’t even real. Some people call it “False Evidence Appearing Real.” The kind of fear you feel when there’s actual danger right in front of you is a gift — it protects you, and you should listen to it. But the fear that imprisons people is almost always the made-up kind: a frightening story we tell ourselves about a future that hasn’t happened and probably never will. We build it in our own minds, then live as though it’s certain. So when fear grips you, learn to ask one honest question: is this a real danger right now, or am I making this up? You’ll be amazed how often the answer sets you free.

Here’s where faith changes everything. When your security is anchored in God, fear loses most of its grip, because you know that whatever happens, you are held. You don’t have to be fearless on your own strength — you just have to trust the One who is.

And there is exactly one fear worth keeping. The Bible says, “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.” That kind of fear isn’t terror — it’s awe, reverence, a deep respect for how big and holy God is. That fear doesn’t shrink your life; it opens it up. Fear God, and you’ll have far less reason to fear anything else.
bible_verse_text: The Lord is my light and my salvation — whom shall I fear? The Lord is the stronghold of my life — of whom shall I be afraid?
quote_text: Let me assert my firm belief that the only thing we have to fear is fear itself.

title: Work to Live
reference_content:
Work to live — don’t live to work. It’s a simple idea, but almost nobody actually lives it, and getting it right early will shape your entire life for the better. So let me press on it a little.

I have met far too many successful, hard-working men and women who, somewhere deep down, deeply regret how much of their lives they poured into their jobs. They climbed, they achieved, they earned — and then they looked up one day and realized the years were gone, the kids were grown, and the moments they can never get back were spent at a desk instead of at home. Almost no one, at the end of their life, wishes they’d worked more. But an awful lot of them wish they’d been more present — for the people they loved, and for the life right in front of them.

Work is good and necessary. God designed us to work, and there’s real dignity and joy in doing something well. But work is a means, not the point. It’s meant to provide for your life, not to become your life. The paycheck is there to fund the things that actually matter — your faith, your family, your friendships, your health, your rest. The moment it flips, and life starts serving the job instead of the job serving life, something precious quietly slips away.

So decide now what kind of life you want to build, and make sure your work stays in its proper place inside it. Make sure the person you marry shares this too — it’s very hard to live this way alone. And someday, teach it to your own kids, not just with words, but by actually being there for them.

Work hard when you work. Then close the laptop, go home, and live. The job will still be there tomorrow. The people you love — and the moments with them — won’t wait forever.
bible_verse_text: For a person may labor with wisdom, knowledge and skill, and then they must leave all they own to another who has not toiled for it. This too is meaningless.
quote_text: Perpetual devotion to what a man calls his business is only to be sustained by perpetual neglect of many other things.

title: Sex
reference_content:
The standard line is that “guys are only after one thing” — they want sex and will do just about anything to get a girl into bed. It’s supposed to be different for Christian men. I hope it is, but honestly, that’s not always the case. You’re a Christian guy, and you’ve been taught that sex is for marriage. The world will tell you something completely different, constantly. So here’s the real question: is it okay to be a man who isn’t only after one thing? The answer is a clear yes — and it’s exactly the kind of man I’m asking you to be.

So how do you actually do that? It starts with who you choose. Pick a girl who shares your values and your expectations. If you don’t, you’ll end up being the one forced to “hold back” against constant pressure — and that’s a genuinely hard place to be. Choose someone walking the same direction as you, and you’ll be pulling together instead of fighting each other.

And understand this: even in a great, strong relationship, sex is not the “next step” toward something more mature. It isn’t a step at all — it’s a gift reserved for marriage. If you refuse to see it as a way to get closer or the next “stage,” it simply won’t be on the table. Anyone who tells you it’s necessary, natural, or required is lying to you. Sex fogs everything. Even the desire for it clouds your judgment; once it enters a relationship, you stop thinking straight. Your purity is one of the most precious gifts you can carry into your marriage someday — and giving it to your wife is worth far more than any “experience” the world tells you you’re missing.

Because you’re not missing anything. There’s no prize for playing the field — only regret to carry later. The right woman someday will be thrilled, not disappointed, that you waited. I promise you: you will have a stronger, deeper marriage if you do.

And one more thing, because grace matters as much as truth: choosing to save yourself is an ongoing decision — one you’ll keep making right up until you marry. Wherever you are, there is always grace, and always my love and support. Come talk to me anytime, about anything. I love you, no matter what.
bible_verse_text: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.
quote_text: There is nothing like desire for preventing the thing one says from bearing any resemblance to what one has in one’s mind.

title: Humility
reference_content:
Let me tell you about one of the most attractive, powerful, and underrated qualities a person can have: humility. The world will tell you to promote yourself, out-shine everyone, and make sure people know how great you are. I want to tell you something better.

First, let’s clear up what humility actually is, because most people get it wrong. Humility is not thinking less of yourself. It’s not putting yourself down, shrinking back, or pretending you have no gifts. Here’s the real definition, and it’s worth memorizing: humility is not thinking less of yourself — it’s thinking of yourself less. That’s the whole secret. A humble person isn’t consumed by how they’re coming across, how they measure up, or what everyone thinks of them. They’re free of all that — free to actually notice other people, to serve, to listen, to love.

Compare that to arrogance, which is the exact opposite. You know the type — the person who talks about themselves endlessly, then says, “But enough about me… what do you think of me?” Arrogant people are trapped inside themselves. And here’s the irony: arrogance is usually just insecurity wearing a costume. Truly secure people never need to look down on anyone.

Humility doesn’t mean you can’t be confident, either. You can be both at once — quietly sure of who you are, and far more interested in others than in yourself. In fact, that combination is exactly what makes someone magnetic. People are drawn to those who make them feel important, not to those who are busy being impressed with themselves.

And this is close to the heart of God. The Bible says again and again that He opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble. Jesus Himself — with every right to boast — chose to serve, to kneel, to wash feet. If that’s how the King of everything carried Himself, it’s a pretty good model for us.

So think of yourself less. Lift others up. Stay humble. You’ll be happier, you’ll be loved, and you’ll look far more like Jesus.
bible_verse_text: God can’t stomach arrogance or pretense; believe me, he’ll put those upstarts in their place.
quote_text: By my count, more business leaders have failed and derailed because of arrogance than any other character flaw.

title: Manipulation
reference_content:
I know the verse and quote for this one are a little heavy — but this is an area I truly believe you, and honestly everyone, needs to watch out for. It’s manipulation.

Here’s the uncomfortable truth: most of us are surprisingly good at it, myself included. Somewhere along the way — probably over many years and many times when it worked — we learn to manipulate to get our way. It takes a hundred quiet forms: not telling the whole story, adding details that aren’t quite true, carefully timing when and how you share information, steering a conversation — all with the goal of getting what you want, keeping what you have, or dodging what you don’t want to face. The reason it’s so dangerous is precisely that it often works.

But here’s what it costs, and the price is steep: manipulation quietly destroys trust with the very people who love you most. They end up feeling used and misled, even if they can’t put their finger on why. And trust is everything. Think of it like a bank account — every honest, straightforward interaction adds to it, and every manipulation quietly withdraws from it. Empty that account, and the relationship is in real trouble.

As a kid, the consequences for manipulating were small — losing your phone, your screen time, a sleepover — handed down by people who love you unconditionally no matter what. But in the adult world, the stakes climb fast: lost jobs, lost relationships, lost people you hold dear. And there’s something bigger now, too. As an adult, you’re building a reputation and a witness that the whole world can see. Guard it.

So here’s my strange advice: make it your goal to be bad at manipulation. Stop practicing it. Get worse at it, on purpose. Choose to be the kind of person who just says what’s true, asks for what they want plainly, and lets the honest chips fall where they may. The sooner you start, the freer you’ll be.
bible_verse_text: ...know for sure that you will be punished for your sin.
quote_text: All sin tends to be addictive, and the terminal point of addiction is what is called damnation

title: The Gift of Being Bored
reference_content:
Here’s something your generation almost never gets to experience, and it worries me a little: boredom. And the reason is simple — the phone. The moment there’s an empty second, it’s right there in your pocket, ready to fill it with a scroll, a video, a game, a feed that never, ever ends. You never have to be bored again. That sounds like a good thing. It isn’t.

I want to tell you why boredom is actually one of the most underrated gifts in life. When I was young, we didn’t have a screen to escape into, so boredom was just part of things. You’d finish everything you had to do, and then… nothing. Empty time, stretching out in front of you. And here’s what I’ve come to realize: that empty time was a gift, even though it never felt like one — because boredom is where the good stuff quietly begins.

Think about what boredom pushes you toward. Bored, you might finally pick up that book. You might learn something new just because you wondered about it. You might create something — draw, build, write, play. You might take the nap your body was quietly begging for. You might notice someone who could use a hand, and go help them. You might have a long, wandering conversation that becomes one of your favorite memories. Almost every good and creative thing I’ve ever done started in a moment when I had nothing to do.

But a phone fills that space before it can ever do its work. You end up entertained every second and creative almost none. Comfortable every moment, and stretched almost never.

So here’s my genuine encouragement, and I know it sounds backwards: put the phone down and let yourself be bored. Don’t rush to fill every quiet moment. When boredom shows up, treat it as an open door. Take the nap. Learn the thing. Help the person. Make something. Or just sit, think, and be still — the Bible says, “Be still, and know that I am God.” Some of the best moments of your life will grow out of the empty ones, if you’ll only let them.
bible_verse_text: Be still, and know that I am God.
quote_text: All of humanity’s problems stem from man’s inability to sit quietly in a room alone.

title: Being An Adult
reference_content:
Congratulations! You are, once again, the youngest — the youngest kind of adult there is. Just when you’d finally made it to the top of childhood, here you are, right back at the beginning of something brand new. And I could not be more proud of you. You have your entire life ahead of you now, to live.

So live it well, and live it as it’s meant to be lived, because it’s the only one you’ll ever have on this earth. One of the ways you prepare for eternity is by living a full life here. I hope one or two of the things I’ve told you in these pages will be of real value to you now. Take the very best and worst of everyone around you, mix it with the very best and worst of yourself over all these years, hold it all up against the Bible for a truth test — and then GO FOR IT.

You have such flexibility and such wide-open opportunity ahead of you. I once saw a license plate that said: “If you’re living as if there is no God… you’d better be right.” That’s true — but I think it’s even better the other way around: if you live as though there is a God, you’re right, so enjoy everything He’s given you. And He’s given you so much already. You are blessed — you really are.

So don’t be afraid to make a mistake. Don’t be fearful. You are loved, cherished, prayed for, appreciated, and accepted exactly as you are. My love for you is unconditional — it always has been and always will be. You did enough to earn all of my heart the very day you were born. You are precious, unique, special, significant, valuable, and wanted. I am endlessly impressed by you — your talent, your creativity, your humor, your confidence, your intelligence. I’ve said it before: you are perfectly imperfect.

The only real problem is that it means I now have a grown child — and I’m quite sure I’m far too young for that! You have given me an unbelievable run of years. They haven’t all been perfect, but through every one of them, I have felt incredibly, indescribably proud to be yours.
bible_verse_text: Don’t stop listening to correction my child, Or you will forget what you have already learned.
quote_text: The future...something which everyone reaches at The rate of sixty minutes and hour, whatever he does, whoever he is.

title: Praying
reference_content:
There’s really only one subject left that I need to share with you. It isn’t the 52nd most important thing — it’s just the last one, and in many ways it holds all the others together. I want to tell you how important it is to pray about everything you do.

I genuinely believe we all need what I call “prayer cover” — people praying for us, and us praying for others and for ourselves. It’s one of the most powerful and most overlooked things in the world. Since before you were even born, I have prayed for you without stopping. I believe with all my heart that it has made a difference, and I want to encourage you to bring absolutely everything to God — your challenges, your fears, your hopes, your wildest dreams.

Here’s the truth about the life ahead of you: it is exciting and wonderful, and it is also, at times, very hard. You cannot do it on your own — and the good news is that you were never meant to. Recognize your place in things: it is by the grace of God that you exist and breathe at all. So talk to Him. Ask Him for what you need. It’s easy to ask, because He is more than worth the asking, and He loves you more than even I do — which is saying something.

I have loved sharing all of these thoughts with you across these pages. And now I’ll ask you for one thing in return: please pray for me, too. I mean it — I need it. It matters more to me than any birthday card you could send or any phone call on a holiday. Just talk to God, and mention me sometimes.

Thank you for these years — every single one of them has been a gift. And God willing, we have so many more still ahead. Until then, and always: pray. It’s the last thing I’ll tell you, because it’s the thing that carries you through everything else.
bible_verse_text: Lord hear my prayer; listen to my cry for mercy. Answer me because you are loyal and good.
quote_text: One single grateful thought raised to heaven is the most perfect prayer.

title: I Got You
reference_content:
Let me just say it plainly, because you and I both already know it: divorce sucks. There it is. No sugar-coating, no pretending otherwise. It’s hard and it’s messy and neither of us would have chosen the pain of it.

But here’s the thing I hold onto: out of all of that suckiness, I got you.

You’re not technically “mine” — I know that. But I get something I consider an absolute privilege: I get to love you. And that’s exactly what this whole book is. It’s me, sharing that love with you, one page at a time.

So I’m going to unabashedly pour my wisdom into these chapters — everything I’ve learned, everything I want for you. I do it in love, with love, and for love. That’s the only reason any of it is here.

I hope you’ll treasure these pages. I hope you’ll come back to them. And whatever else you take from this book, don’t ever forget the simplest, truest thing in it:

I love you.
bible_verse_text: And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose.
quote_text: Love is not something you feel. It is something you do.

title: Don't Compare Yourself to Others
reference_content:
You would figure that the “competition, comparisons, measuring up, cliques, groups, etc.” would be gone once you leave school and step into adult life. You would think the social pressures, and the wondering about what everyone else thinks and does, would finally go away.

It doesn’t.

I have seen far too many people well into adult life who are still comparing themselves to everyone else. They are still trying to keep up with the rich neighbor, the smart relative, the famous schoolmate, or the popular coworker. It is a waste of time and not worth the effort. You can’t win, but you can lose.

The years growing up are rampant with people comparing where they are, where they are headed next, and what they have accomplished. There is always someone who did better than we did, and someone who did worse. The problem is that not everyone started in the same place — and we know for a fact that these years are NOT the finish line.

We have each been given things we can control and things we can’t. You can’t control the fact that you are bright, smart, beautiful (I’m allowed to say that!), and funny, any more than you can control the house or the country you were born into. But you can control how you respond to conflict, hardship, and success — and how you stay committed to God, family, friends, and even enemies.

Expect the best from yourself no matter what your circumstances. Don’t compare your success or failure to others. Measure your "place" against your own dreams and goals, and against what God wants for your life.
bible_verse_text: A sound heart is life to the body, but envy is rottenness to the bones.
quote_text: The truest mark of being born with great qualities is being born without envy.

title: Seeking Advice from Others
reference_content:
They say in business that free advice isn’t worth anything. I disagree. Seeking advice to help you make decisions is critical to your success as an adult — and even now. Finding people who have experience you can draw on to make decisions about your life is really valuable. That advice can steer you in the right direction and help you live the life you were meant to live. The formula I use is simple: take in all advice and measure it three ways.

First, does it match up to the Bible? It is the one place I can always trust. Then I pray about it. Why not get the answer straight from the top? What is cool is that even people who aren’t Christians or Jews live by the truth that is in the Bible. Most don’t even know they are following it.

Second, does the person giving the advice have my best interest in mind? (Note: I first seek advice from people who are close to God. Whenever I am seeking real advice, I always look at what their relationship is like with Jesus at that time. Usually I will ask, “How is your walk these days?” From there I can measure the advice.) Do they like me and care for me? People who love you are a great place to get input. Despite my shortcomings at times, that is why you should always ask me for advice — whether you use it or not.

Third, does this person have a personal interest in the question? If so, then I have to be very careful with their advice. This is especially true in relationships. Seeking advice from — or listening to — a boyfriend, for example, on whether to have sex with him before marriage would be a “bad” place to get advice.

Remember, I am your biggest fan, and I will ALWAYS give you an answer that is in your best interest — even if you don’t like it.
bible_verse_text: “Every word of God is flawless; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.”
quote_text: Successful people follow the same advice they prescribe for others.

title: Character
reference_content:
It’s hard not to be a hypocrite. Everyone ends up being one occasionally. For the most part, we start acting like someone we’re not, or trying to be something we aren’t. We say one thing and do another. We try to impress our friends, hide things from our parents, go along with the crowd, and even show off. Sometimes our bad behavior doesn’t look so bad simply because we’re around people whose behavior is worse. Our own odor, while awful, doesn’t seem to “smell” so bad when those around us are much worse!

But the secret to character — and the true measure of any hypocrite — is how you act when you are alone. You can tell who you truly are when you are by yourself and no one else can see you: when it is just God and you. How you behave in those private moments speaks volumes. Are you honest? Do you hold yourself accountable? Are you the same person alone as you are in front of others? If someone were watching, would you be proud of what you did?

Here’s the thing about character: it isn’t built in the big, dramatic moments. It’s built in the small ones, over and over — the times you tell the truth when a lie would be easier, the times you do the right thing when no one would ever know the difference. Every one of those small choices is a brick, and over the years they build the person you become.

The good news is that it works in your favor. If you practice being honest and good when you’re alone, being honest and good in front of others becomes almost automatic. You won’t have to remember which version of yourself to be, because there will only be one you — the same person, everywhere, all the time. That is what integrity really means: being whole, undivided, the same on the inside as the outside.

And if you are ever looking for someone’s character to emulate — Jesus would be a great choice.

Be a person of character first when you are by yourself. Then, when you’re around other people, it will be much easier — because you’ll already know exactly who you are.
bible_verse_text: Give her credit for all she does. She deserves the respect of everyone.
quote_text: Be more concerned with your character than your reputation, because your character is what you really are; your reputation is merely what others think you are.
quote_attribution: John Wooden - Hall of Fame Basketball Coach

title: Forgiveness
reference_content:
There is probably no stronger attribute a person can have than the ability to forgive and to ask for forgiveness. In many instances it is a very small action on your part, but it has a huge impact on the people you love — and even on those you don’t. The inability to forgive is much harder on you than it will ever be on the other person. When you don’t forgive, you give up control of your peace, your joy, and sometimes your sanity to either the other person or the thing that happened. That is too hard, and way too much to give away.

The most challenging forgiveness for me is forgiving myself. How about you? I do really well when it comes to other people. It is almost easy for me to see the best in them. When you see the best in others — their challenges and their struggles — the things they do to you become much easier to forgive. But it doesn’t always work that way for me. The single hardest thing for me to do is forgive myself. What is crazy is that Christ died on the cross so we could be forgiven. If we don’t forgive others, including ourselves, then what He did was wasted. Even with all that knowledge and comfort, I still struggle in that area.

How are you at forgiving others? Are there things and people you need to forgive? What about yourself? Do you need to ask for forgiveness anywhere? Are you clean there as well? I hope so. I love you too much to have you burdened when the ability to forgive and be forgiven is right there in front of you.

<mark>Just to make sure you are reading these, if you say the word “forgiveness” and give me a high five, I will give you ten dollars.</mark>
bible_verse_text: For if you forgive men when they sin against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
quote_text: Anger makes you smaller, while forgiveness forces you to grow beyond what you were.

title: Treat you like a "Queen"
reference_content:
This is the first in a series about men and boys — the guys you’ll date, and ultimately the man you may marry someday. Consider it hard-won perspective on what you should expect, and what you should never settle for.

Minimum requirement #1: he treats you like a “queen.”

I cannot emphasize enough how important it is that you find someone who treats you wonderfully. You deserve to be treated that way every single day — not just sometimes, not “well, this one boyfriend wasn’t really like that.” All the time is the only acceptable answer. If you settle for less in even one small relationship, you start to believe it’s okay to be treated poorly. It isn’t, and it never will be.

Being treated like a “queen” means you are precious, special, respected, cared for, protected when it matters, and — most importantly — you belong to God and should be treated accordingly. This isn’t hard to recognize. You will know it when you see it, and just as importantly, you’ll know when you don’t.

Here’s something worth understanding: the people you choose to date are, in a way, a reflection of how you see yourself. If you choose someone who is selfish, self-absorbed, and completely focused on themselves, it often reveals that you don’t think you deserve better. You do. Don’t ever hand your time and your heart to someone who doesn’t appreciate you. Does that make sense?

So surround yourself with men who lift you up, who genuinely like you and respect you, and — above all — who draw you closer to Christ rather than away from Him. A man who points you toward God is worth a hundred who only point you toward themselves.
bible_verse_text: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself up for her.
quote_text: No one can make you feel inferior without your consent.

title: Men and their Mom's
reference_content:
Watch how the guys you date treat their mother. It is the best window you will ever have into how they will treat you. If a man treats his mother with kindness and respect, there is a very good chance he will treat you the same way. Think back to when you were growing up — you can probably picture plenty of your friends and how they treated their own moms. Most of my friends were pretty good at it. How were yours?

You can learn an enormous amount about a man by how he treats his mother. Is he kind to her? Does he make fun of her — and I mean mean-spirited, not good-natured teasing? Does he speak to her gently? Does he respect her? Does he lift her up in front of other people, or put her down? Does he honor her? Pay attention, because how he treats the woman who raised him is very likely how he will one day treat his wife.

Here is why this matters so much: he took a lifetime to learn how to treat his mother. Those are deep habits, formed over years, and they don’t just disappear when he meets someone new. People show you who they are over time, in the small moments — not in the way they act when they are trying to impress you.

And while you are watching how he treats his mother, watch how he treats everyone who can’t do anything for him — the waitress, the janitor, the person who makes a mistake. A man’s real character shows in how he treats people he doesn’t have to be kind to.

None of this means you are looking for someone perfect. You won’t find him, and he won’t find a perfect you either. But you are looking for someone whose heart is in the right place — someone kind, respectful, and honoring, especially toward the people closest to him. You deserve to be treated well, every single day. Watch closely, and believe what you see.
bible_verse_text: Honor your father and mother so that you will live a long time in the land that the Lord your God is going to give you.
quote_text: How sharper than a serpent’s tooth it is to have a thankless child!

title: Lying
reference_content:
You’ve probably read a thousand messages on this subject already, so I’ll keep mine simple.

First: tell the truth, if for no other reason than it’s the easiest thing to remember. Lies require upkeep. The truth just sits there, always the same, waiting for you whenever you need it. A liar needs a good memory; an honest person needs none.

Second, a subtle one: not saying something isn’t the same as lying. One of my favorite movie lines is “You can’t handle the truth!” — and the fact is, sometimes people can’t, and sometimes they don’t need to. If a hard truth won’t help, heal, or lovingly correct someone, you’re not required to say it just because it’s true. Choosing to stay quiet, or to be gentle, isn’t dishonesty — it’s kindness. There’s a big difference between lying and simply not volunteering every blunt opinion you have.

Third, and this is the big one: don’t lie to yourself. This is the lie that does the most damage, because you’re the one person you can never get away from. The recovery programs for drinking and drugs have a step about getting out of “denial” — which is just a fancy word for the lies we tell ourselves. Self-deception always gets worse with time, never better. The truth you avoid today will cost you more tomorrow.

And be sharp about what you take in. We live in a world absolutely flooded with untruth — fake stories, doctored images, confident voices online saying things that simply aren’t so. More than any generation before you, you’ll have to work to find what’s real. Don’t be lazy about it. Just because you read it or heard it or saw it doesn’t make it true. Weigh everything against what you know to be right, and against God’s Word, which never changes.

And stay humble. I once read a prayer in a book that stuck with me: “Lord, help me to forgive, and to accept, those who sin differently than I do.” Hold honesty as sacred — it matters more than ever — but be gracious toward others, because you have your own failings too. Guard the truth, tell the truth, and love the people who are still learning how.
bible_verse_text: To fear the Lord is to hate evil; I hate pride and arrogance, evil behavior and perverse speech.
quote_text: A liar needs a good memory.

title: Wow! You are Special
reference_content:
I am so proud of you. There’s really no other way to say it. You are something truly special — far more than I ever could have imagined when you first came into my life. And somehow, you keep becoming more.

The joy you bring me is impossible to measure. There are so many things about you that I love — little things, big things, things you probably don’t even know I notice. I am so deeply blessed to have you as my stepdaughter. Not many people get a gift like you, and I get to keep you forever.

I can’t wait to see who you become as you grow. I can’t wait to meet the person you’ll marry someday. And I really can’t wait to see your own children one day — can you even imagine what your kids will be like? Think about that for a second. Pieces of you, running around, being wonderful.

This book is supposed to be 52 things you need to know. This one is the simplest of them all, and maybe the most important:

You are special, and I love you — VERY, VERY much.
bible_verse_text: My command is this: love each other as I have loved you.
quote_text: To love is to receive a glimpse of heaven.

title: Healthy Eating
reference_content:
“You are what you eat.” It’s a corny saying, but it really is true. Sadly, there are a ton of bad food choices available all day long, and it seems like the more stress and time pressure we’re under, the worse we tend to eat. Learning to eat well is a genuinely valuable life skill. An understanding of nutrition and health will benefit you for your whole life.

Please forgive the analogy, but your body is a lot like a car. If you put the right fuel in it, take care of it, and treat it the way the “manual” says, it will perform great. If you neglect the engine and only worry about how it looks on the outside, you’ll eventually run into trouble. The big difference is this: with a car, you can always get a new one. Your body is the only one you’ll ever have.

Remember that it all works together — eating well, moving your body, and getting enough sleep all add up to a healthy body you can use to chase every one of your dreams and goals. This isn’t about being a certain size. It’s about being strong and well enough to live the life God has for you.

One honest and important thing: a lot of people — of every age — quietly struggle in this area. Some start to see themselves in the mirror very differently than they actually are, and that can lead to deep pain, and sometimes to eating disorders. If you ever feel confused, anxious, or at war with food or your own body, please don’t carry it by yourself. Come talk to me, or to someone who loves you. There is no shame in struggling, and there is real help. You are never a burden for needing it.

Take care of the body God gave you, treat it with respect, and use it to live a full and joyful life. It’s the only place you get to live — make it a good home.
bible_verse_text: Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own.
quote_text: Take care of your body. It’s the only place you have to live.

title: Money
reference_content:
One of the most valuable things a man I worked for ever taught me came in the form of a hard question. One day he looked at me and said, “Why do you choose to be poor?” I didn’t have a good answer, so I told him I didn’t choose to be poor. He said that based on how hard I worked and the job I was doing, I was, in fact, choosing it.

That felt harsh at the time — and honestly, it’s not the whole truth. Not everyone works for money, and money is far from the only thing that matters. Being poor in money doesn’t make you poor in spirit, poor in friends, or poor in the things that actually count. But buried in his blunt question was something real: for many of us, how much we earn really is more of a choice than we like to admit.

Here’s what I’ve learned since. Plenty of people far less clever than me make much more money than I do. And plenty of people far smarter than me make much less. Making money, in a lot of cases, is a decision — about effort, focus, and the value you choose to create. I came to see it as one useful way of keeping score. Not the only way, and definitely not the most important way — but one honest measure of how well you’re doing what you set out to do.

Now here’s the balance, and it matters: money is a wonderful tool and a terrible master. The Bible doesn’t say money is evil — it says the love of money is. Chase it as your scoreboard for life and you’ll never have enough; no amount satisfies that hunger. But earn it honestly, hold it loosely, use it to bless people, and it becomes a genuine gift.

One more principle I lived by: when I left a company, it would be in a sea of red ink or black ink — but never in handcuffs. Earn it, but always keep your integrity worth more than the money.
bible_verse_text: Whoever loves money never has enough; whoever loves wealth is never satisfied with their income. This too is meaningless.
quote_text: Lack of money is no real obstacle; lack of an idea is an obstacle.

title: What Men say...
reference_content:
One of the biggest risks we take when we let someone close is that we start to accept whatever they say about us as fact. Their words become our mirror. That’s fine when the person is kind and honest — but it’s dangerous when they’re not, because the people closest to us have the most power to shape how we see ourselves.

Here’s a truth worth holding onto: the person you marry, or seriously consider marrying, should absolutely find you attractive — and you are (there’s no denying that). But far more important than being loved for how you look is being loved anyway — for who you are, on the days you feel beautiful and the days you don’t.

A relationship built mainly on physical attraction is a shaky foundation. And a relationship where a boyfriend — or, worse, a husband — regularly criticizes how you look is not just shaky, it’s harmful. If a man consistently points out what he thinks is “wrong” with you, runs you down about your body, your clothes, or your face, walk away. It doesn’t matter how confident you are today; hearing that year after year will wear a groove in you. No one is strong enough to be criticized forever and stay unhurt.

Please hear me: you don’t have to earn someone’s kindness by changing how you look. A man worth your time will build you up, not tear you down. He’ll make you feel more like yourself, not less. If someone is constantly telling you to lose a few pounds, dress differently, or fix your face — that’s not love talking, and it’s not your problem to fix. It’s your signal to go.

You were made in God’s image, and you are already enough. Don’t ever let someone else’s words convince you otherwise.
bible_verse_text: What a person desires is unfailing love; better to be poor than a liar.
quote_text: To love and be loved is to feel the sun from both sides.

title: The Perfect College Day
reference_content:
There are 24 hours in a day. Here is what every successful college student figures out — ideally before they ever set foot on campus:

**A Perfect College Day:**
Sleep — 8 hours
School — 3 hours
Eating — 3 hours
Studying — 3 hours
Everything else — 7 hours
Total — 24 hours

If you can figure this out early enough, college will be a genuinely successful experience. You’re given 24 hours every day, and if you can discipline yourself to get enough sleep and study a little every single day, you will do amazingly well. Managing your time is one of the biggest keys to college — bigger than raw intelligence, honestly. Plenty of brilliant people flunk out because no one is making them go to bed or do their work anymore.

Look at that schedule again: even after sleep, class, meals, and studying, you still have seven hours left over every day to have fun, work, join things, and hang out. That’s an enormous amount of freedom. The trick is that the freedom is exactly what makes it hard.

The jump from high school to college is honestly a little alarming. Nobody wakes you up. Nobody checks your homework. Your ability to stay focused in an environment of total freedom is the real adjustment — and it’s where a lot of people stumble. I made sure I went to the library to study, because every time I tried to study in my dorm room I got distracted by everything and everyone. Find your own version of the library — a place where your brain knows it’s time to work.

Study a little every day, protect your sleep, and use your freedom wisely. Do that, and you’ll be amazed how well the rest of college falls into place — including all the fun in those seven hours.
bible_verse_text: There is an appointed time for everything. And there is a time for every event under heaven.
quote_text: Half our life is spent trying to find something to do with the time we have rushed through life trying to save.

title: Pornography
reference_content:
I know this might sound like a strange subject for a parent to bring up — but it’s a serious one, and I’d rather be honest with you than leave you unprepared. Pornography is a massive addiction in this country, especially among men. It is degrading to women, and it’s harmful all the way around. So be aware of it in the guys you date and spend time with, because it really does eat at a person’s brain and fill it with false images and impossible expectations.

A guy who talks to you about pornography, or mentions something he’s “seen” that you should try, is showing you exactly who he is — and it’s the wrong person to be around. This includes magazines, explicit movies, most of what’s a click away on the internet, and anything else that treats women as objects. Sadly, for a lot of men there’s a very short distance from “barely bad” to genuinely sick. It’s an addiction, and addictions only get worse over time.

I also want you to understand what it quietly does to a person. It takes something God designed to be beautiful — real love and real intimacy between a husband and wife — and trades it for something fake on a screen. Over time it teaches a man to compare the real woman he’s with to images that were never real to begin with. That’s a heartbreaking way to live, and an even harder way to be loved.

Here’s what I most want you to know: you are not a collection of images to be rated and compared. You are a whole person, made in God’s image, worthy of real love and real respect. A man who is captivated by fake, unreal women on a screen will always struggle to truly see and cherish the real, wonderful woman standing right in front of him.

Pornography has no place in a healthy relationship — married or otherwise. Stay away from it yourself, and don’t settle for a man who finds it fascinating. You deserve someone whose eyes and whose heart are fully, completely yours.
bible_verse_text: God wants you to be holy and to stay away from sexual sins.
quote_text: All sins are attempts to fill voids.

title: Leadership
reference_content:
It’s hard to teach someone to “give it their best.” That’s especially true in school. Some people never really try, and then feel bitter about the colleges, jobs, and choices they end up with — even though, deep down, they know they didn’t give it their all. You probably know people who are frustrated they can’t get into the school they wanted, yet never actually worked very hard for it. Here’s the truth: your effort counts. Your drive to do well in school can pay off, and it will.

But drive is bigger than grades. Once you know how to work hard — once you’ve felt what happens when you truly pour yourself into something — you’re holding one of the most valuable tools a person can have. The real question becomes: what will you do with it?

Can you apply that same drive to your relationships? To the people and causes you serve? Can you use it to teach others things you’ve already figured out? That’s what leadership actually is — it isn’t a title or a position. It’s taking the effort and ability God gave you and using it to lift other people up.

So let me ask you some real questions. Can you individually change the world? Can you make a difference for Jesus right here on earth? Can you influence a generation, a country, a town, a family — or even just one single person who crosses your path?

The answer is yes.

Not “maybe.” Not “someday, if things go well.” Yes — right now, as you are. God doesn’t hand that kind of drive to someone by accident. He gave it to you on purpose, for a purpose. So work hard, lead by serving others, and go be the answer. The world needs exactly what God put in you.
bible_verse_text: Commit to the Lord whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
quote_text: The final test of a leader is that he leaves behind him in others the conviction and will to carry on.

title: Words
reference_content:
For some reason, the older you get, the more your words matter. As a kid, you get a lot of leeway in what you say. Sometimes being young lets you “get away” with comments that get brushed off as just something a kid would say. But as you grow up, those same words don’t get passed over so easily — and more importantly, the responsibility for what you say changes. As an adult, you’re accountable not just for your actions, but for your words. A complaint, a criticism, a careless opinion — it all carries more weight than it used to.

Words are powerful in a way that’s easy to forget, because they feel free and temporary. But they’re not. A kind word can lift someone for a whole day. A cruel one can stick with a person for years — sometimes for life. You probably remember something hurtful someone said to you long ago, word for word, even if they forgot it the moment it left their mouth. That’s how much weight words carry.
